questionText:
A polygon is convex if, for every pair of points, $P$ and $Q$ belonging to the polygon, the line segment $PQ$ lies completely inside or on the polygon.

Which one of the following is NOT a convex polygon?
explanation:
Definition of Convex Polygon:
A polygon is defined as convex if, for any two points $P$ and $Q$ within or on the polygon, the entire line segment $PQ$ remains completely inside or on the boundary of the polygon.

Analysis of Options:
• Option A: This polygon has an inward notch (a concave indentation). If two points $P$ and $Q$ are chosen near the left indent, the straight line segment connecting $PQ$ goes outside the polygon boundary. Thus, it is a concave (non-convex) polygon.
• Options B, C, and D: These shapes (triangle, square, and trapezoid) are convex polygons, as any line segment joining two interior/boundary points stays entirely within or on the polygon.

Therefore, Option A is NOT a convex polygon.
